title: Mitochondrial variants and donor haplotypes
conclusion: Singlet's genotype-free per-donor mt haplotypes reach precision 0.89 and recall 0.91 against replicate-lane truth on held-out Kang lanes (mgatk on vireo clusters: 0.93 / 0.89). For MAESTER clone-defining variants the 3' per-cell VAF has mean AUROC 0.79 (mgatk 0.79).
methods: Real data with real truth. (1) Kang 2018 lanes: each donor's homoplasmic mtDNA haplotype is taken from a second library of the same donors (cells labelled by the authors' demuxlet calls, mgatk allele counts, AF >= 0.9 and depth >= 20 against rCRS). Singlet's genotype-free per-donor mt variant files (from its own clusters) are compared with it, as are mgatk counts pooled by vireo's clusters, the pipeline a user would assemble. Precision is the share of predicted variants at covered truth positions that are in the truth; recall is the share of truth variants recovered. (2) MAESTER BPDCN712: 26 clone-defining mt variants whose positive cells were established from the paired mt-enriched library of the same cells; for each, the AUROC of the per-cell VAF from the standard 3' library separates positive cells from the other clone cells (both tools on the same alignments and cells; mgatk counts UMI-deduplicated molecules, Singlet counts reads). (3) MAESTER K562 + BT142: agreement of per-line allele fractions from the 3' library with the MAESTER fractions. Singlet is run end to end (default pipeline, automatic donor count); mgatk 0.9.0 runs on the chrM reads of Singlet's BAM for the same cells. Rules are match-or-beat against mgatk with zero tolerance; informational metrics have no competitor. Variants and counts stay private.

tools.name: singlet
tools.params: singlet-campaign POOL.1fq --ref-base /mnt/projects/debruinz_project/cellarium/reference --genome-dir /mnt/projects/debruinz_project/cellarium/reference/GRCh38-2024-A/star_2.7.11b --exons /mnt/projects/debruinz_project/cellarium/reference/GRCh38-2024-A/genes/genes.gtf --threads 16 --pipeline --n-donors -1 --tagged-bam possorted.bam --bam-sort-mode disk --output-format mtx --raw-matrix  (default SNP panel: 1000 Genomes phase 3, AF >= 5%, 7.35 M SNPs; --n-donors K only for the told-K comparison runs)

tools.name: mgatk
tools.params: mgatk bcall -i chrM.bam -n POOL -o out -c 8 -bt CB -b barcodes.txt -ub UB -g rCRS (chrM reads of Singlet's tagged BAM; other options at their defaults: NHmax 1, NMmax 4, base quality 0)

tools.name: vireo
tools.params: cellsnp-lite as above, then vireo -c cellsnp -o OUT -N K -p 16 --randSeed {1,2,3} --noPlot (K = true K, defaults otherwise: nInit 50, doublet detection on); K estimate: vireo -N 12 --randSeed 1, K = donors holding >= 1% of cells

allele counts; variant calling needs its R step

caveats: Haplotypes, variant positions, allele counts and per-site allele fractions are not published; the artifacts hold counts per donor, per anonymised variant and sufficient statistics only.

The Kang haplotype truth comes from a second library of the same donors, counted by mgatk, so mgatk-based predictions share its counting rules; recall is measured against every truth variant, including positions the tested lane barely covers.
Singlet's mt caller was developed on the Kang batch 2 control lane (PR #36); that lane is reported but kept out of the pooled numbers.
mgatk is run with its documented 10x settings (bcall, CB and UB tags, rCRS); its variant calling is an R step that was not run, so heteroplasmic variant lists are not compared, only its counts.

In standard 3' libraries mt reads cluster at transcript 3' ends; only the clone-defining variants with enough coverage are scorable, and the other variants of the MAESTER truth cannot be tested with this data type.
